Verano — Rome, Italy

Relatively safer day Average night

In detail

Verano is home to Rome's largest and most historic monumental cemetery, Campo Verano, a quiet and generally safe place to visit by day. Local press has reported an unauthorised Roma/nomadi encampment of caravans and campers along the cemetery's outer walls near the ring road, described by nearby residents as a persistent source of frustration; this is a degrado/urban-decay issue rather than documented violent crime. No specific safety concerns beyond this localized encampment issue were found.

Frequently asked questions

Is Verano safe?

Wandroz currently rates Verano in Rome, Italy as relatively safer than most other areas covered on Wandroz during the day and roughly average compared to other areas covered on Wandroz at night. This is a qualitative first-pass assessment based on general local knowledge and public reputation, not an official geolocated crime dataset — see the note on data limitations below before treating it as more precise than it is.

Is Verano safe at night?

At night, Verano is rated as roughly average compared to other areas covered on Wandroz. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Verano a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Verano's day rating (relatively safer than most other areas covered on Wandroz) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
